findings.title: Migration interpolates old site setting values into raw SQL
findings.body: The migration builds INSERT statements by interpolating each line from the old embeddable_hosts site setting directly into SQL. A value containing a single quote can crash the migration, and a deliberately crafted admin-set value could execute arbitrary SQL during the migration. Use connection.quote or a parameterized insert.

findings.title: Migration assumes settings rows exist and will crash on many upgrades
findings.body: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category and execute(...)[0]['value'] for uncategorized_category_id. Site settings are often only stored when changed, and the embed_category join may return zero rows. In those cases [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. Use safe access and defaults.

findings.title: Migration does not normalize old embeddable host values
findings.body: The model normalizes hosts by stripping scheme and path, and lookup matches only the URI host, but the migration inserts old setting lines verbatim. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 will be stored with scheme/path and will never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host after upgrade. Blank or whitespace-only lines can also be inserted. Normalize/trim values and skip blanks during migration.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint or validation for hosts
findings.body: Neither the model nor the migration enforces a unique host, including case-insensitive uniqueness. Duplicate hosts can be created in the UI or inserted by the migration. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses an unordered .first, so if duplicates have different categories, imported topics may be assigned to an arbitrary category. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index on lower(host).

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without checking that host is present. Creating or updating an EmbeddableHost with a missing host parameter raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Add a presence validation or guard before mutating the attribute.

findings.title: Host matching ignores ports and may not normalize case
findings.body: The validation allows hosts with ports, and the port is stored, but record_for_host queries using URI(...).host, which excludes the port. Therefore a host saved with a port never matches referers/URLs. The parsed host should also be downcased before comparing to lower(host), otherwise uppercase hostnames may fail to match. Normalize host matching or remove port support.

findings.title: update and destroy do not handle missing records
findings.body: update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call save_host or destroy. If the id does not exist, host is nil and the action raises NoMethodError. A non-numeric id can also cause a database type error. Use find_by(id: params[:id].to_i) and return 404 when missing.

findings.title: save_host assumes params[:embeddable_host] exists
findings.body: save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] and params[:embeddable_host][:category_id] without requiring the embeddable_host hash. A request without that key raises NoMethodError. Use params.require/permit or guard for missing parameters.

findings.title: category_id value of 0 is not treated as uncategorized and is not validated
findings.body: The controller replaces category_id only when blank?, but in Rails 0 is not blank. A no-category value of 0, or an invalid id cast to 0, can be persisted as a dangling category_id. The model also does not validate that the category exists. Treat 0 as uncategorized and validate category existence.

findings.title: Edit action crashes when host category is missing
findings.body: edit() sets categoryId from this.get('host.category.id'). If the category was not hydrated, was deleted, or the stored category_id is invalid, host.category is undefined and clicking Edit throws TypeError. Use host.category_id or safe navigation.

findings.title: Plural embedded id hydration assumes value is an array
findings.body: The new _ids hydration calls obj[k].map without checking that obj[k] is an array; a null or undefined plural id field will throw. It also deletes the original *_ids key even when lookup fails, producing arrays containing undefined records. Guard with Array.isArray and skip or filter missing objects.

findings.title: Existing embeds remain expandable after all allowed hosts are removed
findings.body: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable hosts are configured. If admins delete all EmbeddableHost records to disable embedding, previously imported topic embeds can still be expanded and can still trigger remote fetches via TopicEmbed.expanded_for. If removing hosts is meant to disable embedding, restore a host-allowed check.

findings.title: resources :embeddable_hosts exposes actions that are not implemented
findings.body: The route declaration creates index/show/new/edit routes, but Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only implements create, update, and destroy. Requests to the unused routes will hit missing actions. Use only: [:create, :update, :destroy].

findings.title: Host regex restricts TLD length to five characters
findings.body: The host validation regex requires the TLD to be 2 to 5 letters, which rejects valid modern domains such as example.technology. Consider using a less restrictive hostname validation or URI-based validation.

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no functional tests
findings.body: The added controller specs only assert inheritance from AdminController. There are no tests for create/update/delete, invalid or missing hosts, missing parameters, category assignment, duplicate hosts, or migration normalization. Add functional tests for the new endpoints and model behavior.
